findings.text: The fixture points the crew home at tmp_path/home through RECKON_HOME (lines 54-56) because the live run store made the promotion answer already_promoted, but no assertion proves the real home is untouched; the repository rule for a test that writes outside state says an isolated read does not prove an isolated write, so a later regression that drops the env var reddens this file only by accident of what the machine's store happens to hold, and the durability of the isolation rests on nothing.

The head run is quoted at revision de514aec026cd6bab2a91a0547e974d932d0e3ab while head-gate.log's own header records f47ab32781cfc780c049e853276409e397ffbb82, and line 27 quotes the after arm at de514aec while after-arm.log ran at f47ab32; the figures hold because f47ab32 changes only this html, but the recorded head is not the revision either log was written at, which is the pair a later reader compares against the commits being promoted.

The paragraph states every measurement ran on 98dci4-clu-3142.iter.org, while baseline-arm.log, after-arm.log and negative-control.log record 98dci4-clu-3143 and head-gate.log records 98dci4-clu-3144, and line 12's 'as a batch job on all_debug' has no scheduler receipt beside head-gate.log - the run directory's only .scheduler files belong to the scoped gate and the two suite arms, each reading the bwrap bind-mount refusal - so the partition claim rests on prose that the logs contradict.

The commits field separates the two ids with a space, while the done_when requires plain full commit ids separated by commas; both ids are full and resolve, so the field carries the fact it owes and only the declared shape differs.

The evidence record names the one cause and its measurement but carries no ruff check or ruff format --check result on the changed paths, a done_when clause for which the run directory holds no record at all (a search for 'ruff' over the manifest, this fragment and the four logs returns only the dispatch brief), so one clause of the stated measure is unverified.
